# @displayxr/inline3d — DisplayXR inline-3D web SDK

> Glasses-free 3D for web pages on a DisplayXR spatial display: you render one image per eye into a
> canvas, the DisplayXR Browser weaves them for the panel; an ordinary browser shows the page in 2D.

Read first: docs/making-3d-look-right.md — nine depth and comfort rules from real panels
(the default depth is the glass: centre the subject on z = 0 and frame the first view; tilt flat
arrangements about an axis through the glass, don't push them back; keep moving things' forward swing small, fixed convergence and no near geometry in worlds,
low contrast behind the subject, text as HTML near the glass, no coplanar surfaces, no sub-pixel
detail, a cover that always comes off). The SDK's defaults do the rest.

Pick the view rig before writing code — decide by what the user moves, not by whether the page
owns a camera. The user turns a SUBJECT (model, product, diorama, simulation, chart), even with an
orbit control: DISPLAY rig (keep the orbit camera and pose the portal from it with
displayRig({ position: target, orientation: camera.quaternion, virtualDisplayHeight: 2·d·tan(fov/2) })).
The user moves through a WORLD (first person, game, map, editor, ported VR): CAMERA rig. Then
check depth at three window sizes and in full screen: the subject must stay on the glass.

Four mistakes a page makes most often (each looks fine in a 2D browser):
- a cover over a new canvas comes off on handle.firstWoven (a player's too: player.firstWoven),
  never on 'ready' / loadeddata / the first frame, and always on a timeout as well;
- a splat tile needs an opaque clearColor matching the page: the default transparent clear weaves black;
- an addScene page passes onLayerLost that draws ONE mono view across the canvas, never a no-op;
- page chrome over a tile (sticky header, buy card, caption) is fine as ordinary HTML, opaque or
  translucent, as long as it covers part of the tile; no filter/blend on it, frost only a partial region.

## Reference
- docs/authoring-inline-3d.md — every API, both view rigs, comfort maths
- docs/woven-canvas-rules.md — what the browser does to a woven canvas; CSS, remount and cover rules
- docs/content-lifecycle-rules.md — swapping content in a window: release programs, textures, containers (handle.releaseEntity)
- docs/porting-three-js-apps.md — moving an existing three.js app over
- docs/authoring-motion-and-effects.md, docs/splat-effects.md — motion, reveals, depth envelopes
- index.d.ts, three.d.ts, viewer.d.ts, model.d.ts, splat.d.ts — the public API with JSDoc
- CHANGELOG.md — what changed per release
